candidate.answerReason: The faces containing the edge of length 7 force a face with lengths 7, 36, 41. The other face containing 41 must use 18 and 27, leaving 13 as the opposite edge.

methods.label: Start with the shortest edge
methods.explanation:
Every face of a tetrahedron is a triangle. The edge of length \(7\) is especially restrictive: if the other sides of one of its faces are \(u\) and \(v\), the triangle inequality requires \(|u-v|<7\).

Among the remaining lengths \(13,18,27,36,41\), the only pairs differing by less than \(7\) are \((13,18)\) and \((36,41)\). Both pairs also have sum greater than \(7\). Each edge belongs to two faces, and those faces share only that edge, so the two faces containing the edge of length \(7\) must have side lengths
\[
(7,13,18)\quad\text{and}\quad(7,36,41).
\]
Consequently, one face containing \(AB=41\) has other sides \(7\) and \(36\).

The other face containing \(AB\) cannot reuse either of those edges. Its other two lengths must therefore come from \(13,18,27\). They must have sum greater than \(41\), and
\[
13+18=31,\qquad13+27=40,\qquad18+27=45.
\]
Thus that face must use \(18\) and \(27\).

The two faces containing \(AB\), namely \(ABC\) and \(ABD\), together contain every edge except \(CD\). Their lengths are \(41,7,36,18,27\), leaving \(\boxed{CD=13}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

review.mathematicalCheck: Only the pairs \((13,18)\) and \((36,41)\) can accompany edge 7 in its two faces. Thus one face at edge 41 uses 7 and 36. Its other face must use 18 and 27, the only remaining pair with sum exceeding 41. The opposite edge is therefore 13, choice B.
